lessons.title: Practice Logistic Predict
lessons.description: Implement logistic_predict(x, w, b, threshold=0.5) returning 0/1. The test checks that logistic_predict(10, 1, 0) equals 1; logistic_predict(-10, 1, 0) equals 0.
learning_objectives: Mesa clerks recount crates before dawn, and threshold logistic probabilities.
lessons.starter_code:
import math

def logistic_predict(x, w, b, threshold=0.5):
    # TODO
    pass
lessons.solution_code:
import math

def logistic_predict(x, w, b, threshold=0.5):
    p = 1 / (1 + math.exp(-(w * x + b)))
    return 1 if p >= threshold else 0

lessons.title: Practice k-NN Classify
lessons.description: Implement knn_classify(x, points, labels, k) majority vote of k nearest (1D). Tie → smaller label. The test checks that knn_classify(0, [-1, 1, 2], [0, 1, 1], 3) equals 1; knn_classify(0, [-2, -1, 5], [0, 0, 1], 2) equals 0.
learning_objectives: Orchard clerks recount crates before dawn, and classify with k-nearest neighbors.
lessons.starter_code:
from collections import Counter

def knn_classify(x, points, labels, k):
    # TODO
    pass
lessons.solution_code:
from collections import Counter

def knn_classify(x, points, labels, k):
    dist = sorted(((abs(x - p), lab) for p, lab in zip(points, labels)), key=lambda t: (t[0], t[1]))
    votes = [lab for _, lab in dist[:k]]
    counts = Counter(votes)
    best = max(counts.values())
    winners = sorted(lab for lab, c in counts.items() if c == best)
    return winners[0]

source.name: scikit-learn User Guide — Nearest Neighbors — 'Classification is computed from a simple majority vote of the nearest neighbors'

lessons.title: Practice Checkpoint Precision Recall
lessons.description: Finish precision_recall(y_true, y_pred) so it returns (precision, recall) for the positive class 1. Use 0 when a denominator is 0. The test checks that precision_recall([1, 1, 0, 0], [1, 0, 1, 0]) is about (0.5, 0.5).
learning_objectives: Attic clerks recount crates before dawn, and compute precision and recall.
lessons.solution_code:
def precision_recall(y_true, y_pred):
    tp = sum(yt == 1 and yp == 1 for yt, yp in zip(y_true, y_pred))
    fp = sum(yt == 0 and yp == 1 for yt, yp in zip(y_true, y_pred))
    fn = sum(yt == 1 and yp == 0 for yt, yp in zip(y_true, y_pred))
    prec = tp / (tp + fp) if (tp + fp) else 0.0
    rec = tp / (tp + fn) if (tp + fn) else 0.0
    return prec, rec

tests.name: test_precision_recall
tests.unittest_code:
def test_precision_recall(self):
    p, r = precision_recall([1, 1, 0, 0], [1, 0, 1, 0])
    self.assertAlmostEqual(p, 0.5)
    self.assertAlmostEqual(r, 0.5)

source.name: scikit-learn User Guide — 3.4 Metrics and scoring — precision, recall and f1-score
